items.title: dictyBase is live — tell us what you think
items.body: dictyBase is now open to the whole community as a public beta. This is the new home for Dictyostelium genomes, genes, curation, the Stock Center, and a growing set of analysis tools, and it is free and open to everyone. We built this for you, and we would love your feedback. Try it on the genes and questions you care about, and tell us what works well, what is missing, and what could be clearer. If you hit a bug or find something that looks wrong, please report it so we can fix it quickly. You can reach us any time through Submit corrections and Suggestions under the Community menu. We read every report, and your input directly shapes where dictyBase goes next. Thank you for being part of this. dictyBase belongs to the community.

items.title: How curation works now: whole papers, author review, and honest dates
items.body: A few changes to how dictyBase curates the literature. When a new Dictyostelium paper appears, dictyBase drafts the gene summaries, Gene Ontology terms, phenotypes, and interactions it reports, then invites the corresponding author to check them. Authors get a private link, edit or remove anything wrong, and pick official GO terms from a search box rather than knowing them by heart. Anything they are unsure about can be flagged for a curator instead of confirmed. Nothing becomes part of the curated record until a curator has reviewed it, and you can sign in with ORCID so the work is credited to you. Where a paper is openly available, dictyBase now curates from the full text rather than the abstract. That finds far more of what a paper reports, including controls and negative results. When no open copy exists, a curator can supply one, and the page an author reviews says which was used. The front-page recent papers list now orders by when each paper actually became available, not by journal issue date, so a paper assigned to a later issue no longer outranks newer ones. It shows that date.

items.title: The full screen movie archive, new gene-list tools, and inline FASTA
items.body: The full developmental screen is now on the site. Around 6,500 time-lapse movies play on the mutant strain pages, so nearly every screened clone can be watched developing next to its phenotype scores. This is up from the first small batch. Two new tools sit under Analyze. The batch gene annotator turns a list of genes into a table of GO terms, phenotypes, human orthologs, disease links, expression peak, and protein domains, and you can download it as a spreadsheet. GO-slim mapping sorts a gene list into high-level functional categories. The enrichment and batch tools now accept UniProt accessions, not just gene symbols and DDB_G ids. You can also choose to include uncurated annotations in an analysis: the AI layer, the Gomer Lab annotations, author-submitted curation, and community curation. For the Gomer Lab predictions you set a confidence cutoff. Gene pages can now show a sequence, not just download it. Beside each FASTA download there is a view option that displays the sequence on the page, so you can copy a protein straight into BLAST or another tool. One small fix: clicking a result inside a tool or a search now opens it in a new tab, so your list stays put when you go back.

items.title: New gene page layout, cell-tracking tools, and screen movies
items.body: Gene pages have a new layout. A gene's curation now sits together at the top, just under the record. The dictyBase curated summary comes first, with a link that opens its GO terms and phenotypes. Author, community, Gomer Lab, and AI annotations sit in tiles you can open when you want them. The links to PubMed, AlphaFold, NCBI, and UniProt are tidied into two rows. There is also a new cell tracking page under Analyze, courtesy of David Knecht. It offers TrackMaxima, a Fiji plugin that tracks cells in time-lapse movies, and an Excel template that turns the tracks into speed, directionality, and plots. Both were developed in Robert Insall's lab at the Beatson Institute. The Sawai developmental screen movies now play on the mutant strain pages, so you can watch a clone develop beside its phenotype scores. And dicty.org now points here.

items.title: New this week: a jobs board, feeds, and a numbers page
items.body: A few additions from the past few days. There's a new Jobs & positions board under Community for PhD, postdoc, staff, and faculty roles. Gene pages now link out to InterPro and PDB, and Stock Center strains link back to their gene page. You can follow site news by RSS or Atom. And a new dictyBase by the numbers page shows live counts of the genes, genomes, annotations, and stock the site holds. We also finished a data-accuracy review: it corrected the genomic coordinates shown on the featured gene pages and the totals in the advanced gene finder, and we added automated checks so those stay right.

items.title: Improvements from your beta feedback
items.body: Thanks to suggestions from beta testers: the developmental RNA-seq charts now plot time proportionally, so the intervals match the real course (hourly to 12 h, then every 2 h). Gene pages have a new "Genomic + 1 kb flanks" download that adds 1000 bp up- and downstream for promoter and terminator regions. The qPCR primer tool now lets you set the product size range. And in the Stock Center you can click a strain or plasmid to see its full details before adding it to the cart.

items.title: New genome: Dictyostelium giganteum, now 20 hosted
items.body: The newly published Dictyostelium giganteum genome (Sharma et al. 2026, Genome Biology and Evolution) is now hosted here, bringing the site to 20 sequenced dictyostelid genomes. The assembly (NCBI GCA_059609475.1) and its annotation are in the genome browser, BLAST, the comparative species search, and the Downloads page, with gene models, restriction sites, and sequence downloads.

items.title: Download the sequences behind the genomes
items.body: You can now get the actual sequences three ways. In the genome browser, click any gene model to download its sequence as FASTA. On each D. discoideum gene's Orthologs tab, download that gene's orthologs as protein or CDS, one genome at a time or all at once in a single file. And on the Downloads page, every sequenced genome now has CDS (nucleotide) and protein (amino acid) FASTA files, one record per gene ID. With thanks to Tera Levin for the suggestions.

items.title: Curated protein and genetic interactions on gene pages
items.body: The Interactions tab now shows experimentally curated physical and genetic interactions from BioGRID, each with its experimental method and publication, alongside the predicted associations from STRING. It is a focused set for Dictyostelium today, and curators and authors can help grow it over time.

items.title: Two more dictyostelid genomes, 19 now hosted
items.body: D. citrinum KGL29A and D. intermedium PJ11, two genomes still working through GenBank's pipeline, are now hosted here directly. That brings the site to 19 sequenced dictyostelid genomes. Both are in the genome browser, BLAST, downloads, and the ortholog tables, using the sequencing team's own contig names and gene IDs. With thanks to Tera Levin and the Holland*, Ahmed* et al. 2025 team for sharing the assemblies.

items.title: Curated orthologs, and ortholog search in the browser
items.body: Two ortholog improvements. Each gene's Orthologs tab now shows curated ortholog calls across all the sequenced dictyostelid genomes, from the Holland*, Ahmed* et al. 2025 OrthoFinder groups, each linking straight to its locus in the genome browser, with paralogs flagged. And in the genome browser, typing a gene symbol while viewing another species jumps to that gene's ortholog there. The natural-variation panel now compares each strain against its true ortholog rather than the closest paralog.

items.title: Search by more than one phenotype, and download the results
items.body: Phenotype search can now combine several phenotypes at once. Enter multiple terms separated by a semicolon and choose all (AND) or any (OR), for example chemotaxis; aberrant fruiting body. Every result also has a one-click download of the matching gene list as a spreadsheet.
